newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mostly flat in further consolidation of recent sharp gains. January closed $3 lower at $1.346 per tonne, while March closed unchanged at $1.320 per tonne. Traders said the market's immediate direction would hinge partly on origin sellers. Producers stepped back from the market following the rally, trying to see how far the market would go.

In New York arabica futures closed higher across the board with front-month March adding 25 points to close at 119.60 cents/lb. May closed also 25 points higher at 117.40 cents/lb while the outer months gained between 50 and 80 points.

Traders said that although roasters need to buy coffee to keep up with consumption and replenish stocks, buying interest was tempered by rising futures prices and firm differentials. It was added that a decline in next season's arabica output coupled with growing consumption in producing countries would likely keep stock levels low through the second half of 1997 and may force roasters to switch their buying strategies. It was added that the recent unexpected drop in US certified coffee stocks underscored nearby supply woes.

BRAZIL - The head of the Primary Commodities Department at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry will meet exporters within Brazil's Coffee Exporters Federation (FEBEC) on January 13 to discuss the progress of exports. By January 13 there should be a final figure for December exports, expected to close at around 1.55 million 60-kg bags, it was said. As of January 8, December shipments based on bills of lading were 1.53 million bags. A figure of 1.55 million bags would bring total shipments in the July/December period to just under the 9 million bags allocated under the ACPC retention scheme.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 75,405 bags of coffee in November 1996, nearly 19 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 811,400 bags, 2.6 per cent more than was imported the same year-ago period. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.4 per cent to 814,700 bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Indonesia (137,800 vs 100,600 bags), Vietnam (156,700 vs 169,500 bags) and Papua New Guinea (229,000 vs 206,000 bags).

SINGAPORE - Singapore imported an estimated 106,760 bags of coffee in August 1996, 38 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 945,200 bags, sharply down on last year's figure of 1.288 million bags. Imports in calendar year 1995 dropped to 1.9 million bags, down from 2.9 million bags in 1994. However, not only imports, but also exports are sharply down. Total exports in January/August 1996 reached 926,000 bags, down from 1.290 million bags the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped to 1.9 million bags, down from 2.8 million bags exported in 1994.
